summary.headline: India Shelter Q2 FY27: Gross AUM Rs. 11,997 crore (+26% normalized YoY), PAT Rs. 146 crore (+19%), collection efficiency back to 98%.
summary.overview: Disbursements rose 21% YoY to a record Rs. 1,126 crore, and management says the momentum is continuing into H2. Asset quality was stable quarter-on-quarter, with GNPA at 1.5% and 30+ at 5.2%, but credit cost for H1 was about 60 bps, driven by a scheduled write-off of about Rs. 6 crore. ROE was 17.3% at 3.1x leverage, and management reiterated FY27 guidance while acknowledging that the 1Q disbursement-accounting transition weighed on AUM growth. Rating upgrade and cost of funds repricing were the main open questions.

segments.name: Home loans vs LAP
segments.commentary: Balance sheet is ~68% home loans against a regulatory expectation of 60% at balance-sheet level; PBC requirement ~63%. Management plans ~57-58% HL share in incremental mix; LAP is ~44% of AUM per analyst question. Home loan and LAP NPA gap is 10-15 bps.

segments.name: Ticket size bands
segments.commentary: Average ticket size ~Rs. 10-11 lakh (inched up to Rs. 11 lakh). Management says ~88% of loans are below Rs. 15 lakh, unchanged from prior disclosure. Sub-Rs. 8 lakh ticket shows the most stress but has ROE above 20%.

segments.name: Customer mix and geography
segments.commentary: Self-employed customers are 75-80% of portfolio. MP demand is weaker after guardrails; Karnataka improving. About 750 pin codes out of ~8,000 have tightened underwriting.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: 40-45 new branches, spreads above 6% in medium term, credit cost 40-50 bps (management says 50 bps for FY27), gross AUM growth 25-30%.
Management guides FY27 disbursement growth around 20% or above and AUM growth 25-27% (normalized); Q3 expected to exceed Q2.
Opex to gross AUM expected to improve ~15 bps YoY in FY27 despite H1 increase.
Cost of funds: ~35-40% repo transmission expected over medium term; rating upgrade expected to cut cost by 15-20 bps; new disbursements (30-35% of AUM) can be repriced.
Overall PAT growth guidance of ~25% depends on direct assignment volumes recovering.
capex_capacity: Branches: none opened in Q1 FY27, ~8 opened in Q2 per management (analyst cited 5); plan of 40-45 branches for FY27 implies a heavy H2 opening program.
Digital sourcing rose to 7% of disbursements in Q2 FY27 from 4% in Q2 FY26; management plans to scale significantly.
Rs. 1,400 crore+ undrawn sanctions and liquidity above Rs. 700 crore; ALM positive across all buckets.
Borrowings from more than 30 counterparties; NHB share stable at 14%; average tenure above 8 years.
demand_pricing: Disbursement run-rate averaged ~Rs. 375-380 crore/month in Q2; management says ~Rs. 400 crore/month needed for H2 targets.
Q1 disbursement accounting moved to clearance basis, reversing ~Rs. 350-400 crore of disbursements and trimming the AUM denominator (about 3.5-4% of growth).
Sanction ratio at ~50%, tighter due to underwriting tightening on sub-Rs. 8 lakh tickets.
Co-lending largely dormant: CLM-1 model and GST on co-lending excess interest make it unattractive; management not keen for now.
Direct assignment: ~12 partners; DA priced ~15-20 bps above regular cost of funds; DA ~17.5% of gross income, targeted ~18%.

qa_highlights.question: How will credit cost fall to ~30-35 bps in H2 to meet full-year guidance, given H1 was ~55-60 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is seasonally higher and Q2 included a ~Rs. 6 crore scheduled write-off of accounts over 2 years old; FY27 credit cost now expected at 50 bps, within the 40-50 bps range.

qa_highlights.question: How will the rising rate environment affect cost of funds and spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds transmits ~40% of repo moves historically; rating upgrade could cut 15-20 bps; new disbursements can be repriced; 53% of portfolio is variable or semi-variable (15% variable, 38% semi-variable converting over 3 years). Spreads expected to remain above 6%.

qa_highlights.question: Why were there no branches opened in Q1 and what is the FY27 branch plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was used for changing disbursement booking mechanism; ~8 branches opened in Q2; the company expects to reach 40-45 branch openings in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress by geography or ticket size, and what actions were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Stress concentrated in sub-Rs. 8 lakh tickets; ~750 pin codes out of ~8,000 tightened underwriting; MP normalizing and Karnataka improving; home loan vs LAP NPA gap only 10-15 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the rating upgrade?
qa_highlights.answer: Rating vintage is ~2-2.5 years since last upgrade, and agencies (India Ratings, CARE, ICRA) typically look for 3 years; management is pitching for early upgrade and expects it in about a quarter or so.

qa_highlights.question: What explains lower direct assignment income despite similar DA volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to portfolio characteristics (residual maturity, spread, customer profile), not to a change in approach.

risks_watch: Credit cost: H1 ~60 bps against FY guidance of 40-50 bps; H2 needs substantial improvement.
30+ DPD at 5.2% on an upward longer-term trend; management has no explicit target beyond sustaining and improving QoQ.
Cost of funds pressure from rate hikes; ~45% of borrowings are bank/MCLR-linked with limited near-term repricing.
IRDA insurance commission draft regulation could reduce non-interest income; management says impact is limited.
Drought in Tier 2/3 markets; 750 pin codes under tighter underwriting; any collection stress would be a key indicator.
Disbursement and AUM growth must reach ~Rs. 400 crore/month and ~25-27% growth to meet guidance; Q3 October disbursement not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term growth trajectory and guidance, but cautious on asset quality and cost of funds. Management repeatedly deferred specifics (October disbursement numbers, rating upgrade timing, 30+ target) and gave few numbers on the LAP industry mix and competition, relying on H2 seasonality.
key_quotes: Gross AUM has reached Rs. 11,997 crores, a normalized growth of 26% year-on-year, and we remain well on track to achieve our FY30 Gross AUM target of Rs. 30,000 crores.
So, if the repo rate will go from here, so we will see some impact on the cost of fund. But there are multiple levers, which can offset the impact of this change in cost of fund.
We are continuing with our guidance that probably we will see Opex to Gross AUM improving by about 15 basis points this year as well year-on-year basis.
Ashish Gupta: So, we have given our guidance, including direct assignment transactions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Opex to AUM guided to improve ~15 bps YoY in FY27, and a rating upgrade could cut cost of funds 15-20 bps, but credit cost is running ~60 bps in H1 against a 50 bps full-year view and NIM is only stable above 9%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 disbursements rose 21% YoY to Rs. 1,126 crore and management guides AUM growth of 25-27% normalized, but the Rs. 375-380 crore/month run-rate must rise to about Rs. 400 crore/month for H2 targets.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or plant plan was discussed; the company is an NBFC expanding through branches and digital sourcing (7% of disbursements), so a capex announcement is not a relevant trigger.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held and AUM growth was effectively narrowed to 25-27% from 25-30%, with credit cost at 50 bps and PAT growth of ~25% dependent on direct assignment recovery.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 credit cost is ~60 bps against FY27 guidance of 40-50 bps, 30+ DPD is 5.2% on an upward trend, and Q3 October disbursement was not disclosed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed; co-lending is dormant and digital sourcing is scaling within existing products.

rows.label: Rating upgrade cuts cost of funds 15-20 bps
rows.why: Rating is ~2-2.5 years old versus the usual 3-year vintage; management expects an upgrade in about a quarter, and the 15-20 bps saving depends on the agencies acting.

rows.label: Direct assignment volumes recover
rows.why: DA is ~17.5% of gross income (target ~18%) and ~15-20 bps above cost of funds, and the ~25% PAT growth guidance depends on DA volumes recovering; ROE is ~16% excluding DA versus 17.3% reported.

rows.label: Cost of funds repricing from repo transmission
rows.why: Cost of funds is 8.2% and transmits ~40% of repo moves; 38% of the portfolio is semi-variable converting over 3 years, but ~45% of borrowings are bank/MCLR-linked with limited near-term repricing.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term growth trajectory, branch program and spreads above 6%, but cautious on credit cost (~60 bps in H1), 30+ DPD at 5.2% and cost of funds, and deferred the October disbursement numbers, rating timing and 30+ target.
